text:
The man prevails. The right-of-way was an easement appurtenant extinguished by merger when the woman conveyed the house to him and he held both the dominant and servient estates, and an extinguished easement does not revive on a later sale. The warranty deed created no new easement, and none arose by necessity or implication: the path was only a more direct route, and the man never possessed or used the house.
CONFIDENCE: 86
